clue.text: Profanity is anything but considerate

indicators.note: anything but considerate means the word considerate is turned into something quite unlike itself, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that swearing is the very opposite of thoughtful behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anything but' reads as plain emphasis, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of 'considerate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecration is violation of something sacred, which is what profanity means in its religious sense.

clue.text: Decline to let passengers alight

definitions.meaning: a decline is a fall or reduction, as in a sudden drop in sales
to set down riders from a car or bus at their stop

explanation.definitionFit: A drop-off is a sharp decrease, and to drop off riders is to set them down from a vehicle.

clue.text: Material that didn't stand out

definitions.meaning: a fabric or cloth
remained seated inside rather than standing outdoors, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't stand out' suggests something inconspicuous, but split it: someone who didn't stand outside sat in.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy woven fabric; split in two it gives the phrase for staying seated indoors.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: warm in the sense of friendly and hearty
a fruit-flavoured beverage or liqueur

explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means heartily friendly, and a cordial is also a sweet drink, often diluted fruit syrup in Britain.

clue.text: Charged a couple of hundred and exploited

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them are CC
exploited means used, taken advantage of

explanation.surface: Someone was billed for two hundred pounds and feels taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' reads as billed money, but it is the legal sense: formally accused of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone charged with an offence has been formally accused of it in court.

clue.text: Lack of information on Grecian styles

indicators.note: styles here is a verb, saying the words on Grecian are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint about having too little data on ancient Greek fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'styles' looks like a noun about Greek fashion, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange 'on Grecian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is the state of not knowing, a want of knowledge or facts.

clue.text: Assurance given about one new tranquillizer

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the word for assurance goes round the other letters

parts.note: nerve means confidence or assurance, as in having the nerve to do something
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A patient is reassured when handed a fresh calming medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: NERVE goes round IN, giving NERV-IN-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that calms or soothes the nerves, a sedative.

clue.text: Ceramicist without money becomes a schemer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ceramicist surrounds the money letter

parts.note: a potter is a maker of ceramics
L stands for pound (libra), the British unit of money

explanation.surface: A penniless pot-maker turns to scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking money, but it means outside: POTTER goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter devises secret plans or conspiracies, as a schemer does.

clue.text: And with forty pounds a year; (Goldsmith)

definitions.text: And with forty pounds a year; (Goldsmith)

parts.words: And with forty pounds a year; (Goldsmith)
parts.note: complete the line from Oliver Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village about the village parson, who was the two missing words with that small income

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a quotation to finish: Goldsmith's parson was described as wealthy enough on forty pounds a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old expression meaning exceedingly wealthy, used ironically of the parson's modest stipend.

clue.text: Know how to dance and spell

parts.note: can means to be able to, to know how to
to trip is to dance or step lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Someone is skilled at dancing and at spelling words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like writing words correctly, but it is a magic charm; a cantrip is a Scottish word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a Scots term for a magic charm or witch's trick, an incantation.

clue.text: Heavenly baked pudding and jam tomorrow

definitions.meaning: read literally, a pastry dish placed up above in the heavens
a promised good thing that never arrives, from Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass

explanation.walkthrough: 'jam tomorrow' is a British idiom for a pleasant reward that is always promised but never delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an unrealistic hope of future reward, and literally describes a pastry floating in the heavens.

clue.text: Fleeced for a small cornet

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a cornet is a brass instrument, a kind of horn

explanation.surface: Someone was swindled into paying for a little ice-cream cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cornet' suggests a British ice-cream cone, but here it is the brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has been fleeced has had its wool clipped off.

clue.text: Still employed as a domestic

definitions.meaning: still working, not yet retired or discharged, as a machine kept running
working as a household servant

explanation.definitionFit: Equipment still in use is said to be operating, and a household servant was said to be employed in this way.

clue.text: Popular Caribbean leader is an unbeliever

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Fidel Castro, the longtime leader of Cuba

explanation.surface: A well-liked Caribbean head of state is said to be an atheist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caribbean leader' looks like a first letter, C, but it means Fidel Castro of Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone who rejects a particular religion, a non-believer.

clue.text: Discourage fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone tries to put off a man who does the cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' reads as a person, but it is a cleaning substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent such as washing powder or soap.

clue.text: Manure one removed from a black hole

parts.note: dung is animal manure

indicators.note: removed suggests the word one is displaced and its letters moved into another order

explanation.surface: Someone is digging muck out of a dark pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' looks like taking away, but it signals rearranging 'one' to EON. 'black hole' is an old term for a prison cell, as in the Black Hole of Calcutta.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground prison, and a black hole was the term for a punishment cell.

clue.text: Ginger-headed youngsters sparkle

indicators.note: headed means only the head, the first letter, of Ginger is taken

parts.note: a litter is a group of young animals born together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger-headed' reads as red-haired, but it means the first letter of Ginger, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is a bright, shimmering light, the same as sparkle.

clue.text: Pressing for a moment

definitions.meaning: urgent, demanding immediate attention
a very short space of time

explanation.definitionFit: Instant once meant urgent or importunate, and as a noun it is a split second.

clue.text: Further publication is about to result

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
an issue is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A new edition is said to be imminent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as 'will soon', but 'is' and 'to' are links and 'about' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a new printing or release of something published before.

clue.text: Frenchman and I tucked into meat from Belgium

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the other letters go within the word for meat

parts.note: flesh is meat
M is short for monsieur, the French title for a man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and the speaker eat Belgian meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it means placed inside: M and I go into FLESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish describes Flanders, the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium, and its people.

clue.text: Penalty points gained by subtle handling

parts.note: a fine is a penalty paid in money
SSE, south-south-east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A team earns penalty points through clever play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' looks like score points, but it is a compass point, SSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is refined skill or delicacy in dealing with a situation.

clue.text: Fitting situation for a friar

definitions.meaning: appropriate, proper, as in all is correct
a friar belongs to a religious brotherhood such as the Franciscans

explanation.definitionFit: In order means proper or appropriate, and a friar is a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Tories involved in local amendment

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for a local pub

parts.note: a local is a British pub near home, an inn

indicators.note: involved means tangled or twisted, so the letters of Tories are mixed up

explanation.surface: Conservative politicians are caught up in a change to council rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like an adjective, but it is British slang for a nearby pub. 'involved' rearranges TORIES to SERTIO before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An insertion is something added into a text, which is one kind of amendment to it.

clue.text: Blows to the jaw

definitions.meaning: strikes, as in karate ...
... is slang for the jaws or mouth, as in licking one's ...

explanation.definitionFit: Chops are cutting blows with the hand, and chops is also a slang name for the jaws.

clue.text: Visible proof of the boatbuilder's skill

definitions.text: Visible proof of the boatbuilder's skill

parts.words: Visible proof of the boatbuilder's skill
parts.note: a single word means both skill and a vessel, so the boat itself is the evidence of the builder's art

explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill in making things and also a boat, so the boat displays the skill.

clue.text: Good gracious! He's framed a cathedral cleric

indicators.note: framed means enclosed, so the letters of He's surround the rest

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Shock that a man has falsely incriminated a church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' suggests a false accusation, but it means surrounding. Ven (Venerable) is an archdeacon's title, and archdeacons serve cathedrals.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavens is an exclamation of surprise, like goodness me.

clue.text: Be fully prepared to offer support

definitions.meaning: to wait ready for action
to back or remain loyal to someone

explanation.definitionFit: To stand by is to be ready for action, and also to remain loyal and back someone.

clue.text: Where tenants pay rent punctiliously

definitions.meaning: rent goes to the landlord, the person who lets the property
exactly, with precise attention to detail

explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is someone who lets property, the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely, in every detail, and literally names the landlord as the destination of rent.
